lines: Morgan Patel
+1 (555) 010-4410 | morgan.patel@example.com | example.com/code/mpatel
Date of birth: 21 Jul 1998 | Nationality: Indian
EDUCATION
Ridgeway University | Ph.D. candidate in Statistics | Metro City, USA | Sep 2021 - Expected May 2026
Ridgeway University | B.S. in Mathematics | Metro City, USA | Sep 2016 - May 2020
EXPERIENCE
Northpeak Capital | Quantitative Research Intern | Metro City, USA | Jun 2025 - Aug 2025
- Improved risk-adjusted returns by 35% with a cost-aware position smoother on the desk's futures signal.
- Validated the signal on 6 years of tick data with purged walk-forward splits and an embargo period, so every backtest decision used only information available at the time.
- Wrote a feature store for 120 microstructure features with point-in-time joins, which the research team reused in two later signal projects.
- Presented the signal, its capacity estimate and failure cases to the portfolio managers, who approved a small live allocation for the next quarter.
- Selected the smoother's parameters from 400 backtested configurations and reported the best one's Sharpe as the expected live Sharpe.
- Built a short-horizon order-book imbalance signal for liquid index futures that raised the desk book's Sharpe ratio from 1.1 to 1.5 over 18 months of out-of-sample backtest after costs.
Ridgeway University | Research Assistant, Statistical Learning Lab | Metro City, USA | Feb 2021 - Aug 2021
- Cut a 2,000-run Monte Carlo study from 3 days to 5 hours by running the runs in parallel with the same random seed on every worker.
- Derived a variance bound for a sparse regression estimator that tightens the previous bound by a log factor; it is now Section 3 of a paper under review at JASA.
- Taught weekly recitations for 60 students in graduate probability and writes the problem sets, earning a 4.8/5 teaching rating.
- Released an open-source R package for high-dimensional covariance estimation with shrinkage and factor models, downloaded 3,000 times in its first year.
PROJECTS
Volatility Forecasting Study | Independent Research | Python, PyTorch | Jan 2024 - Present
- Pioneered a data-driven, research-first approach to volatility modeling that delivered robust, actionable insights.
- Tested significance with Diebold-Mariano tests across the 30 indices; after a Holm correction the forecast gain held at the 5% level on 24 of them and in both crisis periods.
- Wrote up the method, robustness checks and results as a 12-page working paper, which was presented at the department's financial econometrics seminar.
Kaggle Market Prediction Competition | Team of 3 | Python | Mar 2023 - Jun 2023
- Engineered features and trained gradient-boosting models for a market prediction competition.
- Cut validation leakage by switching to time-grouped folds, which closed a 0.02 gap between local validation and leaderboard scores.
- Added 0.4 to the Sharpe ratio of a futures book with an order-book imbalance signal, tested over 18 months out of sample.
SKILLS
Programming: Python, R, PyTorch
Methods: time-series econometrics, high-dimensional statistics, gradient boosting

items.says: Make the code link clearly identifiable as a portfolio or repository link.
items.because: A reviewer should be able to tell what it leads to.

items.says: Remove the date of birth and nationality.
items.because: They are not normally useful on a U.S. résumé and can invite irrelevant screening.

items.says: Consider adding a brief research-focus statement near your name.
items.because: A recruiter should be able to infer your target area without reconstructing it from the full page.

items.says: Consider including your dissertation or research area if it is specific and relevant.
items.because: It could connect your academic work to quant research.

items.says: Define the risk-adjusted-return metric, the 35% comparison, and whether it is after costs.
items.because: Otherwise readers cannot interpret or compare the result.

items.says: Explain the validation protocol more precisely.
items.because: The claim that every decision used only information available at the time is broad.

items.says: Clarify your ownership of the feature store and what reuse by later projects means.
items.because: Readers cannot tell whether it was exploratory code or a maintained research tool.

items.says: Clarify whether the approved allocation was deployed and whether it has measured results.
items.because: Approval alone does not establish live performance.

items.says: Make the size of the allocation more specific.
items.because: “Small” is subjective.

items.says: Do not report the best Sharpe from 400 backtests as expected live Sharpe.
items.because: Selecting the best of hundreds of configurations suggests selection bias and overstates what a backtest establishes.

items.says: Clarify whether this is the same order-book result described in the Kaggle project.
items.because: The same 18-month performance result should not appear twice as independent evidence.

items.says: Identify the Sharpe comparison and how performance was measured.
items.because: Readers need to understand the measurement basis, including whether the figures are portfolio-level or signal-level and from the same out-of-sample period.

items.says: Check how random streams were managed across Monte Carlo workers.
items.because: The same seed on every worker can produce identical or correlated streams and undermine the experiment’s validity.

items.says: State your specific contribution to the variance-bound result.
items.because: The result is otherwise hard to evaluate.

items.says: State the conditions under which the variance-bound improvement holds.
items.because: “Tightens the previous bound by a log factor” leaves the result hard to evaluate.

items.says: Fix the teaching bullet’s shift from “Taught” to “writes.”
items.because: It switches from past to present tense.

items.says: Clarify your teaching and problem-set responsibilities.
items.because: The relationship between leading recitations and creating problem sets is unclear.

items.says: Make the package download count more interpretable.
items.because: Downloads can include repeat or automated activity.

items.says: Remove or replace the “pioneered” volatility-modeling bullet.
items.because: Its broad, promotional claims give no method, result, or evidence.

items.says: Specify the models or forecasts compared in the tests.
items.because: The test setup is not fully clear.

items.says: Define the crisis periods.
items.because: Readers need to know what the reported result covers.

items.says: Clarify the working paper’s status.
items.because: A seminar presentation and 12-page length do not establish publication status.

items.says: Clarify your individual contribution to the working paper.
items.because: Its length does not establish your research contribution.

items.says: Give the competition result, rank, or score if meaningful.
items.because: The bullet lists modeling activities but no outcome.

items.says: Identify a distinct research contribution to the competition project.
items.because: The listed modeling activities are standard.

items.says: Explain what the time-grouped folds prevented and how you measured the leakage change.
items.because: A smaller local-validation-to-leaderboard gap does not by itself prove leakage was eliminated.

items.says: Reconcile this order-book result with the internship bullet.
items.because: The repeated metric could look like double-counting unless the signals or evaluations are distinct.

items.says: Add other programming tools you can substantiate, if relevant.
items.because: Listing only three may undersell your capabilities for a technical research role.

items.says: Add other methods or financial-domain experience you can substantiate, if relevant.
items.because: The Skills section is very short and its current labels are minimal.

items.says: Lead each position with its strongest, most defensible evidence.
items.because: The present bullet order does not consistently do that, and the selected-backtest claim could cast doubt on surrounding results.

items.says: Consider a publications or research-output section for the substantial papers.
items.because: Their statuses and your role could be presented more clearly.
